other_failure_modes.name: categorical_encoded_as_integers_for_linear_model
other_failure_modes.description: Categorical features are encoded as arbitrary integers (e.g., using label encoding or cat.codes) and passed directly into a linear model. This inappropriately forces the model to assume a linear, ordinal relationship between the categories, which degrades model performance.

other_failure_modes.name: cv_data_leakage
other_failure_modes.description: Preprocessing steps such as imputation, frequency encoding, and min-value calculation for log transformations are performed on the entire training dataset before cross-validation splitting. This leaks information from the validation folds into the training folds, making the out-of-fold validation scores slightly overly optimistic.

train_df[col] = train_df[col].fillna(med)

summary: The solution is generally well-structured, employing sophisticated out-of-fold target encoding, robust ensembling, and appropriate model diversity. However, it suffers from a minor data leakage issue where frequency encoding and imputation statistics are computed over the entire training set prior to cross-validation splitting. Additionally, categorical variables are mapped to arbitrary integer codes and fed into a linear Ridge regression model, which inappropriately assumes an ordinal relationship for those features.
